01 / THE SPECIES

A BEAR LIKE NO OTHER

ICONIC FOR
A REASON.

Black. White. Unmistakable. The giant panda is a bear built for life in China's mountain forests, with powerful jaws and a remarkable appetite for bamboo.

A modified wrist bone acts like a thumb, helping pandas grip stems while they eat. Small adaptation. Big advantage.

02 / THE HABITAT

A WORLD
ABOVE
THE CLOUDS.

Cool air. Steep slopes. Endless green. Giant pandas inhabit temperate mountain forests in China's Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Gansu provinces.

Here, bamboo is more than a meal. It's the foundation of an entire way of life.

03 / FIELD NOTES

GET TO KNOW THE DETAILS

A QUIETER
KIND OF WILD.

01 What's on the menu?

Bamboo makes up almost all of a giant panda's diet. They eat shoots, leaves, and stems, spending much of the day feeding to meet their energy needs.

02 Do pandas live in groups?

Adult pandas are generally solitary. They use scent marks to communicate, and come together during the breeding season. Mothers care for their cubs.

03 Can pandas climb?

Yes. Pandas are skilled climbers. Cubs often use trees as a refuge, while their strong limbs and claws help them navigate their forest home.

04 Why the black and white?

Their distinctive coat helps them blend into a patchwork of snow and forest shade. Their dark ears and eye patches may also help with communication.

04 / THE FUTURE

IUCN STATUS VULNERABLE

THEIR FUTURE.
OUR MISSION.

Conservation has helped giant pandas recover. But fragmented forests and a changing climate still threaten their home. Protecting connected habitats gives pandas—and the wildlife around them—room to thrive.
